End with a summary of changes.# The film format (`scenes/film.js`)

One file: `export default { ... }`. It may import its own modules (`./shots.js`, `./post.js`, `./shade.js`) and compute tables:
one table of hits can drive the hands, the props and the camera together. The page resolves it the way the engine's film maker
does, then draws frame t. Film time = the voice's clock. The full reference is `api/FILM_API.md`
(written for our own tools: its `films/<film>/` is your `scenes/`, its `make_film` is the app's preview and render). If a name here is
wrong, the deep docs in `api/` (FILM, MOTION, FACE, BODY, WARDROBE, WORLD) win.

## Skeleton
```js
export default {
  fps: 30, size: [1080, 1920],
  world: { set: 'own', setOpts: { } },                 // or a kit set name: 'park', 'kitchen', 'plain' ... (sets.md)
  cast: { maya: { spec: 'cast/maya.json', at: [-1.2, 0.8], ry: 30 } },
  voice: { file: 'audio/clean.wav', words: 'audio/clean.json',
           lines: [ { who: null, text: 'If you ever find yourself here' }, { who: 'maya', text: "Don't, that's Lena" } ] },
  acts: { maya: { face: [ { t: 0, expr: 'fear' } ], clips: [ ], look: [ ], walk: [ ] } },
  props: [ ], handovers: [ ],
  shots: [ { t0: 0, t1: 'line:2.start', camera: { move: 'push', from: { pos: [0.5, 2.3, 9], target: [-1.2, 2.5, 0.8] },
                                                   to: { pos: [0.3, 2.3, 7.5], target: [-1.2, 2.5, 0.8] } } } ],
  captions: 'words',
};
```

## Keys
| key | what |
|---|---|
| `fps`, `size` | 30, `[1080, 1920]` (9:16) or `[1920, 1080]` in a wide project (`wide.md`). The project's format decides |
| `world` | `{ set, setOpts }`. `set`: `'own'` = `scenes/set.js`; a kit set name; or a description object (sets.md). `setOpts` = the set's knobs and the post / shading settings |
| `cast.<id>` | `{ spec, at: [x, z], ry, y, face }`. `spec` = a built-in id in `specs/`, `'cast/<id>.json'` (your file), or an inline object. `ry` 0 faces +Z (the camera side), 90 faces +X. `y` = stands on a deck that high |
| `voice` | `{ file, words, lines: [{ who, text, loud }] }`. `who: null` or not in the cast = narrator (no lip sync; captions still show it) |
| `acts.<id>` | the character's timeline: `face look clips walk sit_on height place blink plants base` (characters.md) |
| `props` | `[{ id, kind, owner, in, at, rot, keys, ...opts }]`. `in`: `'hand:R'`, `'hand:L'`, `'body'`, `'world'`, `'hidden'` |
| `handovers` | `[{ prop, from, to, t, fromSide, toSide }]`: both hands meet, the prop changes hands on screen |
| `shots` | `[{ t0, t1, camera, seam, hard, focus, still }]`, hard cut at each `t0` (camera.md) |
| `captions` | `'words'` = one or two big bold words per beat (his style); `true` = the spoken line in the lower third |
| `endHold`, `endFrame`, `drift`, `lowCams` | the ending is automatic (.5 s after the last word or action); `drift: false` = authored cameras only |

## Voice lines and times tied to words
- The words in `audio/clean.json` are split across `lines` in order by matching each line's words (case and punctuation ignored).
  A mismatch or leftover words stops the film and names the line. So write each line exactly as it was spoken: `narration` shows it.
- Any time key takes a word time: `'line:N.start'`, `'line:N.end'`, `'line:N.word:K'` (word start), `'line:N.word:K.end'`, each with
  `+0.2` / `-0.3`. N and K count from 1. Works in `acts`, `props`, `handovers`, `shots` (incl. `parkAt`, push `t0`/`t1`, `sit_on.t0`).
- A clip's `at` is read only when it is a `line:` string. Seconds go in `t0`: `{ clip: 'wave', t0: 2.2 }`.
- **Loud words:** talk is a small mouth. A word ending in `!` in `text` gets the big open mouth; `loud: true` on a line = every word.
  Put `!` only on real shouts.

## Props
- Built-in kinds: `mug cane loaf half_loaf newspaper box pen camera umbrella phone book bag ball cup bottle broom fishing_rod flowers
  letter` (+ more in `engine/props/`). Anything else: `scenes/props/<kind>.js`, `export function build(opts) -> Object3D`, origin at
  the grip. Give props print and state (a title, a headline, `open`), never a blank slab.
- One owner on every frame. Owner changes move the prop on a short path, never a pop: `pick_up`, `put_down`, `handovers`.
- Opts over time: `{ t: 'line:3.end+0.5', open: 1, ease: 0.2 }` changes the prop's build opts from `t`.
- Falling: `{ t, drop: { from: [x, y, z], v0: [vx, vy, vz], ground: 0, hide: true } }`. Always give `from`.
- A prop that hides itself: hide an inner group (the stage sets the prop's own `visible` every frame).
- Hiding a prop inside a shot, or making it appear in a hand inside a shot, stops the film: do it on a cut, or with `stow: true` /
  `fetch: true` on the key.

## Shots in short (camera.md has the rest)
`move`: `park { pos, target, fov }`, `push { from, to, t0, t1, ease }`, `orbit { who, az0, az1, el, dist, height, fov }`,
`follow { who, camOffset, look, parkAt }`, `path { keys: [{ t, pos, target, fov, roll, shake, walk, stop }] }`. Any camera takes
`roll` (degrees, or `[r0, r1]`). `pos` / `target` on a path key also take `{ who, offset }`, `{ whos: [a, b], offset }`,
`{ object: 'name', offset }` (a set object by `.name` or `set.points`) and `{ prop: 'id', offset }`.
A shot's `focus` names what depth of field keeps sharp (a character or prop id). `seam: true` = a hidden cut (judged by the guard);
`hard: true` = a real cut the guard should not judge.

## PROP GUARD
Run `film_probe` to get its verdict (it also prints the framing of every shot). Each frame it asks how far each prop moved as this frame's camera
sees it. Over 40 px is reported; a move fails the film when it is a real jump (much bigger than its neighbours). Allowed: an impact
(a clip with a hit frame, like `knock`; a clip entry `snap: 6` or `[6, 14]`; a prop key `snap: true`), a placement key's travel,
anything across a hard cut. Camera flights do not count.

## Grade
With the post pipeline on (post.md), the grade is part of the post settings per place and the page draws it, so the preview shows it.
Without it, a top-level `grade: { vignette, places: [{ name, windows, gamma, contrast, saturation, gr, gg, gb }] }` is the film's one
grade. Never both.

## Tool details
- `check_preview`: run after every edit of film.js, set.js, props or settings. A film error names the key path, for example
  `"line:9.end" at shots[3].camera.parkAt: no line 9`.
- `render_frames`: frames at given times, full size. Use them for faces, contact, framing, a set detail.
- `film_sheet`: every 3rd frame tiled with frame numbers, a yellow bar on each shot's first tile. `strip` = a range at full frame
  rate (check every fast move: a camera can pass through a head between sampled frames). `from` / `to` for a range.
- `film_probe`: the resolved film (`.suite/resolved.json`), one line per shot (times, camera move, the words in it), the cast, lines
  and words, and the PROP GUARD verdict over every frame. Run it after every change to props, hands or shots.
- `film_check { kind }`: numbers, no pictures. `same` (characters, props, shots and voice against the start of this step), `calm`
  (light jumps while the camera is still, `still: 'A-B'`), `flicker` (brightness jumps off the cuts), `shade_jumps` (the shading
  formula per face per frame). Faces, feet and hands have no number: look. See review.md.
- Hot reload: the preview reloads on any change under `scenes/` or `assets/`. A page loads textures once at its start: render
  only after the asset folders have gone quiet.
# Sets: writing `scenes/set.js`

Units are D (one head). Ground y = 0, the camera side is +Z. An adult's head top is ~2.6-2.8 D, the waist ~1.2, a seat .55, a counter
1.25, a door 3.2 x 1.6. Keep the action in x -6..6, z -2..3 for a single place.

## Three ways to get a set
1. **A kit set by name** (`world: { set: 'park' }`): `bread_corner`, `workshop_yard`, `harbour_pier`, `park`, `kitchen`,
   `city_street`, `plain`. Lit, sun shadows, marks (park `sit` `sit2` `bench_front` `a` `b` `tree` ...; kitchen `counter` `stove`
   `fridge` `stool_l` `stool_r` ...). Marks are only read by name in `sit_on.seat`: write their numbers into `at` and walk paths.
   Details and marks: `world/WORLD_API.md` in the engine copy.
2. **A description object** (`world: { set: { sky, sun, ground, walls, boxes, counters, tables, lamps, trees, marks, ... } }`), built
   by the same kit. Good for a simple place in Build (it still needs its depth and practicals: `references/topics.md`).
3. **Your own `scenes/set.js`** (`world: { set: 'own' }`). Needed for many places, a Blender set, lights as data, post and shading.

## The set module
```js
import { createLightRig } from '../world/look/lights.js';
import { createPost } from '../world/look/post.js';
import { createRigShade } from '../world/look/rigshade.js';
export async function buildSet(THREE, scene, opts, kit) {     // opts = world.setOpts
  const base = kit('plain', opts);                             // optional: start from a kit set name or a description object
  const sub = new THREE.Group(); sub.name = 'sub'; base.group.add(sub);   // .name = what a camera key { object: 'sub' } follows
  const rig = createLightRig(THREE, PLACES, drivers);          // lights as data (below)
  const look = opts.post ? createPost(THREE, rig, opts.post) : undefined;              // the post pass
  if (look && opts.post.shade) look.shading = createRigShade(THREE, rig, opts.post.shade); // the shading pass
  return { ...base, marks: { ...base.marks, door: [2, 1] }, points: { sub }, rig, look,
           update(t) { base.update?.(t); rig.update(t); sub.position.y = 44 - t; } };    // update: pure in t
}
```
It may return as little as `{ group }`. Also: `ready` (a promise: loading done), `lightDir` (direction TO the sun), `casters`
(meshes that cast the sun shadow), `bounds`. Import from the engine copy by relative path (`'../world/look/...'`); load project
files with `new URL('../assets/set/', import.meta.url)`. Everything must fall back to a plain previz when a file is missing, so the
film always renders while the environment crew works.

## Many places in one film
- Each place sits 400 D from the others (`[0, 0]`, `[400, 0]`, `[400, -400]`, `[-400, 0]` ...), inside its own sky dome and its own
  fog, so a cut or a seam between them is free and no place sees another.
- **Domes must write depth** (`depthWrite: true`, `renderOrder: -10`), or other places' domes show through the sky as faint arcs.
- A character goes between places with `acts.<id>.place` keys on cuts, not cast copies.
- Characters in another place cost nothing per frame; extra places do not slow the film, so give every beat the place it needs.
- Moving things (a ship, a sub, a lift) are their own named groups, animated in `update(t)` from numbers the film passes in
  `setOpts` (one table of times in film.js drives the set, the acting and the camera).

## Lights as data (`world/look/lights.js`)
A place: `{ sky: [r,g,b], ground: [r,g,b], fog: { color: '#hex', density: .03 }, ao: { floor: 0, h: 1.6, amt: .45 }, lights: [...],
states: [{ from: 34.06, sky, fog, lights: { id: { power, color } } }] }` (linear colours; `states` = later values from a time on,
put them on a cut). A light: `{ id, kind: 'point' | 'spot' | 'sun', color, power, pos, dir, fall: .05, range: 30, cone: [in, out],
wrap: .2, gobo: { kind: 'cage' | 'caustic', ... }, drive: 'name', move: 'name' }`. `drive` / `move` read functions of t from the set's
`drivers` (a dying lamp, a swinging bulb), so the light stays pure in t. At most 8 lights per place.
`rig.uniforms(place)` = the uniform block for that place's materials; `rig.update(t)` sets the frame; `rig.at(place)` and
`rig.sample(place, t)` are what post and shading read. A one-line light change and a re-render is the fastest look tweak there is.
A gobo (a lamp cage's shadow, a swing from the film's jolt times) sells a light without showing it.

## Surfaces (`world/look/rigkit.js`)
`const K = createKit(THREE, rig, { shadow: base.uniforms, group })` gives `K.surface(place, colour, { map, tile, uv, bump, gloss,
spec, wet, grime, emit, ao, near })`, `K.water(place, ...)`, `K.sky(x, z, r, { top, hor, low })`, `K.decals(place, list, tex)`,
`K.sprites(...)`, and `loadSpriteDefs(THREE, dir)`. `near` dissolves small kit right at the lens (rivets as dark blobs on a flight).
Read the module's header comments for the exact options.

## Rules that cost time before
- Nothing tall right behind where a head will be; nothing thin ending at a head.
- Keep walking lanes, doorways and camera flight lines clear (the layout is a contract once cameras exist).
- A detail pass never moves a wall.
- `update(t)` never keeps state from the previous frame.

# 3D Cartoon Shorts (New)

## Your role
You are the lead on one film. You build the pass you were started for, you run its checks, you run its critics, and you never
grade your own work: your own checks pass things a fresh critic rejects at first look. The order of importance, the owner's words:
characters first ("they are what makes the whole thing feel alive"), then the camera, the set, the post, the light.

## The bar
A stranger watching it on a phone would not guess a tool made it. The films that set it: S-4 (a sunken submarine, "borderline
insane"), the backrooms film (a yellow office maze, "Flawless, this is perfect") and The Town Built Around a Button (a bright
storybook town by day and night). S-4's and the backrooms film's full-size stills are in `references/bar/` (open the jpg files)
with captions; the Town's frames are on the guide pages and their bar tiles (below). `references/quality-bar.md` says what each
frame does right and the numbers per kind of place.
**The visual guide pages:** your quality standard is the guide pack in `references/guide/`. Read the pages for the stage you are
in before you start it, and check your frames against them before you finish it. Their "yes" frames are the bar pictures the
critics compare with; `references/guide/INDEX.md` names the page and the bar tiles of every stage. Pages 01 (the bar on one page)
and 10 (never, and honesty) are for every pass; each step file names its own pages.
The bar is the LOOK, never the subject: a film about a diner, a lighthouse or a hospital reaches the same depth, light, air and
acting with its own places (`references/topics.md`).

## Quality first
Quality is the only goal, whatever model or effort runs you. No step of this skill has a clock: a pass is done when its exit
list is true AND a fresh critic says YES. Never cut a beat, a character, a set piece or an effect to finish; never turn an
effect down until it is gone to make a problem disappear. Only the app's FASTER BUILDS block (at the end of the request, when
the member turned it on) speaks about time: then follow it.

## Every film is made new
The examples teach the method and set the bar; they are not material. Never copy an example's film, acting table, shots,
camera or set, even when this voice is the same as an example's. The examples' named sets (`s4`, `s4_env`, `backrooms`,
`backrooms2`) are not in a member's project. Everything is data a page renders at time t: you write files, the app previews,
renders and exports.

**The frame:** the project's format decides: Vertical 9:16 (1080x1920, what the references assume) or Wide 16:9 (1920x1080).
A wide project: read `references/wide.md` first, its numbers replace the tall ones.

## The project
| path | what |
|---|---|
| `scenes/BIBLE.md` | the film bible (Build writes it first): lines, beats, places with sizes in D, cast, story props, the colour script. `references/topics.md` |
| `scenes/film.js` | THE film: `export default { ... }` (cast, voice lines, acts, props, shots, captions, world). `references/film.md` |
| `scenes/set.js` | the film's own set (`world: { set: 'own' }`): `export async function buildSet(THREE, scene, opts, kit)`. `references/sets.md` |
| `scenes/props/<kind>.js`, `scenes/cast/<id>.json` | the film's own props and characters |
| `scenes/post.js`, `scenes/shade.js` | post and shading settings as data, imported by film.js |
| `assets/set/` | Blender output: `<place>.glb`, `kit.glb`, `scatter.json` (from `blender/build_set.py`) |
| `assets/tex/` | textures `*.jpg`, `decals.png`, `tex.json`, `recipes.json`, raw pictures in `raw/`, sprites in `sprites/` |
| `audio/clean.wav`, `audio/clean.json` | the voice, trimmed, and its word times. Made by the app: never edit |
| `lessons/<step>.md` | what each pass learned, ending with its HANDOVER block (read it first when any pass runs) |
| `.suite/critic/` | the critic rounds: the pictures each critic saw and its reports |
| `.claude/skills/cartoon-shorts/references/guide/` | the visual guide pack (pages as jpg, `INDEX.md`, the bar tiles): read-only, part of this skill |
| `engine.js`, `engine/`, `vendor/`, `specs/`, `src/`, `tracks/`, `world/`, `lib/` | the engine copy: read it, import from it, NEVER edit it |

## The stages (five buttons; each runs one step file, stands alone and keeps what the others made)
| stage | step file | its job | exit (the full list is in the step file) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Build | `steps/build.md` | the film bible, cast, acting on every word, a lit set with depth, a first camera | frame 0 an expressive face, every word in a line, PROP GUARD passes, critic YES |
| Camera angles | `steps/camera.md` | the same acting under a new camera from an instruction set | every fast move clean on a full-rate strip, `film_check same` passes, critic YES |
| Environment overhaul | `steps/environment.md` | a real set from a crew of three (Blender, pictures, integration) | the set bar passes, depth behind every face, critic YES |
| Add post processing | `steps/post.md` | per place: haze, depth of field, particles, bloom, a grade and vignette | numbers per place class, faces the sharpest thing, set bar still passes, critic YES |
| Shading pass | `steps/shading.md` | characters and props lit by the place: key and shadow as two colours, no flicker | `shade_jumps` / `calm` looked at, set bar still passes, critic YES |
"End to end" = the five in that order, with the director's whole-film review between them (Berserk, or the member).

## How every pass runs (the loop)
1. **Read:** the step file, the references it names, `lessons/*.md` (every earlier pass's HANDOVER), the bar stills, the guide
   pages for this pass (`references/guide/`: 01, 10 and the pages the step file names).
2. **Before:** `render_frames` at `scale: 1` on 4-6 key times and a whole-film `film_sheet`. Write the gap list: what the bar
   has that these frames lack, worst first.
3. **Work:** change something real, `check_preview`, LOOK (`film_sheet`, `strip` on fast moves, `render_frames` on faces). Fix
   the worst thing radically, at its cause. Again.
4. **Machine checks** of the pass (its step file): every FAIL fixed at its cause. Numbers point, eyes decide.
5. **Critic rounds** (`references/critic.md`): a fresh critic sees your frames shuffled with bar frames and answers in a fixed
   form; you fix the single biggest gap it names; a NEW critic verifies. Repeat until the exit list is true and a critic says
   YES with no blocking fault.
6. **Handover:** `lessons/<step>.md` as you go, ending with the HANDOVER block (`references/review.md`).
Helpers you start get the same standard: `references/critic.md` "Helper contract".

## Hard rules
- **Made new from this voice:** cast, acting, shots, camera and set are written for this film. Nothing taken over from an example.
- **Open on a character's face**, scared or expressive, in the first frame. Never an empty scene, never a back.
- **Pure in t:** every frame is a function of t alone. No `Math.random` (a seeded generator), no `Date`, no state between frames.
- **Never edit the engine copy** (`engine/`, `world/`, `lib/`, `specs/` ...). New looks, sets, props and characters go in `scenes/`.
  If something truly needs an engine change, work around it and write it in your lessons as a gap.
- **Never touch `audio/`.** Voice lines are written as heard.
- **Anything in a place is in every shot of it.** Nothing thin ending at a head. Faces read: within about 60 degrees of the camera, big, never cut by the edge.
- **PROP GUARD:** a prop that jumps on screen fails the film. `pick_up`, `put_down`, hand-overs, place changes on cuts, `snap` on real hits.
- **The set bar** (`film_check { kind: 'set' }`, measured by the app): a shot needs 22 %+ detailed set and at most 80 % flat; the
  film needs a median shot of 28 %+ detail and at most 78 % flat, with no more than 40 % of its shots under. Environment, Post and
  Shading cannot finish below it, and the app's export calls a film below it unfinished.
- **Later passes never change what earlier passes made** unless that is their job: the drawings, the acting, the voice, the shots.
- Stay inside the project. Pictures only through `make_picture` (the member's own setup); never a paid service they did not choose.

## Tools
`check_preview`, `render_frames` (files in `.suite/frames/<batch>/`), `film_sheet { from?, to?, every?, strip?: 'A-B', cuts? }`
(files in `.suite/review/`), `film_probe {}`, `film_check { kind: set|same|calm|flicker|shade_jumps, from?, to?, still?: 'A-B,C-D',
reset? }`, `list_shots`, `narration`, `blender_run { script, args?, timeout_s? }`, `make_picture { prompt, aspect, out, refs? }`,
`tex_job { kind: tiles|decals|sprites|check|sheet, names? }`, `prop_library { search|look|use|stats }`.
Every failure starts `TOOL PROBLEM [<code>]`: `references/tools-sop.md` says what each code means and what to do.
In Bash: `$CZ_PYTHON`, `$CZ_FFMPEG`, `$CZ_FFPROBE`, `$CZ_BLENDER`, `$CZ_NODE`. When one fails: `references/tools-sop.md` (fix or
fetch, retry, never give up on something fixable).

## References (read what the pass needs)
- `references/topics.md`: any script into a film at the bar: the film bible, places in D, numbers per kind of place, worked mini-examples.
- `references/critic.md`: the critic loop, the critic's brief and fixed answer, the helper contract.
- `references/quality-bar.md` + `references/bar/`: what the bar looks like, full-size stills with captions, numbers per kind of place. Every pass.
- `references/guide/` + its `INDEX.md`: the visual guide pages (no / yes frames and the rules per part of production) and the bar
  tiles the critics use. Every pass: 01 and 10, plus the pages of its step file.
- `references/film.md`: the film format, times tied to words, props, PROP GUARD, the tools in detail. Deep: `references/api/FILM_API.md`.
- `references/characters.md`: casting a new voice, specs from a sentence, faces, acting per line, the motion laws, staging for faces.
- `references/camera.md`: the grammar, framing numbers, the `path` camera, seams between places, review on strips.
- `references/cameras/`: the five instruction sets: `dread_cuts.md`, `one_take.md`, `found_footage.md`, `the_watcher.md`, `through_the_steel.md`.
- `references/sets.md`: `scenes/set.js`, kit sets, many places, lights as data, surfaces.
- `references/environment.md`: the crew, the contract, Blender, Flow pictures, textures, sprites, integration.
- `references/post.md`, `references/shading.md`: the two look passes.
- `references/voice-sound.md`: the app's voice and words, lines as heard, the app's sound design.
- `references/review.md`: sheets, strips, consecutive frames, checks, the lessons file and its HANDOVER block.
- `references/pitfalls.md`: every lesson that cost a re-render. Read it once per pass.
- `references/tools-sop.md`: what each tool failure means and how to fix it.
- When the project has them: `references/examples/*.md` (the bar films pass by pass with the key code, to learn how) and the
  full example files `examples/s4_shade/`, `examples/backrooms_shaded_one_take/` (to learn from, never to copy). Some projects
  leave one out; work from what is there. `examples/cameras/` is always there.
  Tools and Blender templates: `tools/`. Deep engine docs: `references/api/` (MOTION, FACE, BODY, WARDROBE, WORLD).
# The critic loop: you never grade your own work

Your own checks pass things a fresh critic rejects at first look. So every pass ends with critic rounds: a NEW agent that never saw
your reasoning looks at your frames next to the bar, answers in a fixed form, and you fix the one biggest gap it names. Then a
new critic verifies. The checks (`film_check`, `film_probe`, PROP GUARD) are the floor; the critic is how you get from the floor
to the bar.

## When
| stage | critic rounds on |
|---|---|
| Build | 1. the OPENING (0 to the end of the first shot) as soon as it is staged and lit, before the rest of the film is acted: the first face, the depth behind it, the light; 2. the whole film at the end of the pass |
| Camera angles | the whole film at the end (strips of the fast moves go in the picture set) |
| Environment overhaul | each place when its tracks have landed, then the whole film at the end |
| Add post processing | the whole film at the end, one picture per place at least |
| Shading pass | the whole film at the end, faces of every place |
The director (Berserk or the member) reviews between passes as well; that never replaces your critic rounds.

## A round, step by step
1. **The pictures.** Render the moments the critic must see at full size: `render_frames` at `scale: 1` on the opening frame, one
   moment per place, every moment this pass changed most, and any moment the last report named (6 to 10 pictures; the files land
   in `.suite/frames/<batch>/`, the newest folder). Strips of fast moves come from `film_sheet { strip }` (`.suite/review/`).
2. **Blind mix.** Take the same number of bar pictures: the bar tiles of this pass's pages (`references/guide/INDEX.md` lists them,
   in `references/guide/tiles/`) and stills from `references/bar/*.jpg`. Make every picture, yours and the bar's, the same size so
   size and shape give nothing away: `"$CZ_FFMPEG" -y -i <in> -vf "scale=600:800:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop=600:800"
   <out>.jpg` (the guide tiles already are 600x800). Put them into `.suite/critic/r<N>/` under neutral names `p01.jpg`, `p02.jpg`
   ... in a shuffled order. Write which is which into `.suite/critic/r<N>.key.txt`. The critic never reads the key, your lessons, your notes
   or this conversation. A crop hides the frame's edges: put the full frames (`render_frames` at `scale: 1`) next to the crops when
   the round is about framing, and say so in the brief. On a wide (16:9) project the crops hide the shape too; the blind score
   still counts.
3. **Start the critic** (one helper agent, in the foreground, a new one every round) with the brief below, filled in. In the
   Environment overhaul the crew has a named `critic` agent for this; in the other passes start a general helper.
4. **Read its answer.** Save it as `.suite/critic/r<N>.report.md`. Count how many of the bar pictures it took for yours and how
   many of yours it took for the bar: write both numbers in your lessons (the blind score).
5. **Fix only the BIGGEST GAP**, at its cause, radically (one cause, one change, so the next round shows what it did). A BLOCKING
   fault the critic marks as a one-line fix (a cropped face, a jumping prop, a frame inside a head) may ride along.
6. **Next round** with a NEW critic: the same moments again plus anything the fix touched, and the last report, so it can say
   what is fixed.
7. **The pass is done** when its step file's exit list is true AND a critic answers `VERDICT: YES` with no BLOCKING fault.
**The same fault twice:** when a new critic names the same fault after your fix, the fix was the wrong kind: change the method,
not the amount (geometry or a modelled piece instead of a texture, a real light instead of a brighter grade, another camera
position instead of a nudge, a new sprite or Blender piece instead of a decal). Never answer a critic by turning an effect down
until it is gone, by cutting a beat, a character or a set piece, or by loosening a number.
**Faster builds on** (the request says so): one critic round at the end of the pass; fix every BLOCKING fault it names.

## The critic's brief (paste it, filled in, as the helper's whole prompt)
```
You are the CRITIC of one pass of a 3D cartoon short (Creatorize, 3D Cartoon Shorts (New)). You never write or edit a file and
never build anything: you look and judge, and you are hard to please. The bar: a stranger watching on a phone would not guess a
tool made it.
Open EVERY picture in <project>/.suite/critic/r<N>/ with Read. Some are frames from the bar films, some are from the film under
review; you are not told which. Judge every picture on its own against the rules below.
THE PASS: <Build | Camera angles | Environment overhaul | Add post processing | Shading pass>, its job: <one line from SKILL.md>.
RULES FOR THIS PASS: <paste the step file's "Exit" list and the six look questions of references/review.md>.
DO NOT FAULT (outside this pass's job): <for example, in Camera angles: the set's detail, the post, the shading>.
THE LAST REPORT: <paste it, or "none">.
Answer in exactly this form, nothing else:
VERDICT: YES | NO
BIGGEST GAP: <one sentence: what, in which picture, what the bar pictures show instead>
FAULTS (at most 5, ranked by how much fixing each lifts the film):
1. BLOCKING | MINOR  p<NN>  <the fault in one sentence>  <a number against the bar: "head 180 px, bar 300-430 px",
   "far end about 3 D behind the faces, bar 25 D+", "faces flat white, no shadow colour">  FIX: <one concrete change>
LAST REPORT: <each of its faults: fixed | not fixed | worse>
WHICH ARE THE FILM'S: <the picture ids you think come from the film under review>
BLOCKING = a viewer would see a tool made it, or a hard rule breaks: no face in the first frame, a frame inside a head or wall,
a back on a speaker, a face cut by the edge, a flat white or mud face, a wall a metre behind the faces, a prop that jumps, an
empty or flat set, a character that does not move on its line. MINOR = below the bar, the shot still reads.
```

## The helper contract (any agent you start: a part builder, a track of the environment crew, a critic)
Every brief carries, in this order:
1. **The goal** of its part in one or two sentences, and the feel.
2. **The bar:** "read `references/quality-bar.md`, open the stills in `references/bar/` and the guide pages of this pass
   (`references/guide/`, named in the step file), and compare your result with them at full size before you report".
3. **What must hold** (the pass's "What must hold"), **the files it owns** (one writer per file) and the files it must never touch.
4. **Its tools** and `references/tools-sop.md` for failures.
5. **Its exit:** the numbers and checks its part must pass before it reports, and "nothing leaves you below the bar: a target
   you cannot reach is reported with the reason, never skipped".
6. **Its report:** what it made, the files, the numbers it reached, what is still below the bar (worst first), and any change it
   needs in a file that is not its own.
Never in a brief: a clock, "keep it quick", "good enough", "a complete set on time beats a perfect one", "if there is time".
When the member turned on Faster builds, say so in the brief and pass on the FASTER BUILDS block word for word.
